prompt:
Build and run a voice-over set for one game character in this project. Create a frame named "Mira ES scenes" holding exactly 17 independent text to speech nodes, one per line below, each labeled with its id. Use the same backend, model, voice and settings on every node: ElevenLabs text to speech, the model ElevenLabs Eleven v3, the stock catalog voice "Narration :: Warm & Inviting :: Pleasant :: Nikki (F)" (Warm, Measured, and Clear), stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, style exaggeration low or default, speaker boost on, normal speed, mp3 output at 44.1 kHz. The lines are in Spanish: if the node has a language setting, set it to Spanish (es); otherwise leave it automatic. It is the same character who speaks English elsewhere in the game, so keep this one voice on every node and let it speak natural, fluent Spanish. Speak exactly the quoted text, with no added words, tags or sound effects; the delivery notes in parentheses are guidance only and must not be spoken. Run every node, then report a table with the columns Label | Node ID | Status | Error | Output fid, one row per line, the label in bold (for example | **radio-1** | ... |) and the fid in backticks.

Lines:
radio-1 (a message recorded into a field radio, composed and direct): "Aquí Mira. Si cruzaste la puerta detrás de nosotros, escucha."
radio-2 (a message recorded into a field radio, composed and direct): "Los celadores quieren una dirección sellada en sus tres placas, y solo sellan a los infractores."
radio-3 (a message recorded into a field radio, a little wry): "Se quedaron con mi orbe en la ventanilla. Recupéralo si puedes."
radio-4 (a message recorded into a field radio, resolute): "Seguimos por la puerta lejana, más allá de su barrera. Sigue la luz."
camp-1 (quiet journal dictation at the end of a long day): "Día quince. Al alba, las islas se juntan a la deriva, y cruzamos con cuerdas mientras se tocan."
camp-2 (quiet journal dictation, matter of fact): "Todas las cuerdas se rompen a nuestro paso. Quien nos siga necesitará los puentes de los constructores."
camp-3 (quiet journal dictation, a fond smile in the voice): "Campamento en la última isla. Nyra habría revisado cada nudo dos veces."
ice-1 (recorded in the cold, practical and steady): "Grabé nuestra señal en el hielo, donde la nieve no pueda enterrarla."
ice-2 (recorded in the cold, practical advice): "No te detengas en el hielo fino. La flecha señala el anillo."
castle-1 (recorded, calm and warm): "Dejé la dirección del castillo para quien me siga. Solo responde en orden."
castle-2 (recorded, calm and clear, naming each step): "Primero el agua, luego la espiral de raíces y después la media luna sobre los árboles."
castle-3 (recorded, warm, a little wistful): "Es el último acertijo que te dejo. Después, el mar."
reunion-1 (live and close, overwhelmed with relief, almost a whisper): "Nyra."
reunion-2 (live and close, tender, holding back tears): "Sabía que seguirías la luz. La mantuve encendida en cada puerta."
reunion-3a (live and close, warm and hopeful): "Trajiste nuestro mapa. Esta vez elegimos juntas la próxima travesía."
reunion-3b (live and close, warm and hopeful): "El camino a casa está abierto. Quédate a mi lado para la próxima."
reunion-4 (live and close, a smile in the voice): "Vamos. Hay más puertas."
